abstract.text: A MusicXML parser, normalizer, validator, and formatter.

inlineContent.text: normalizer, validator, and formatter written in Swift. It targets
back to 1.0, with a strict-concurrency-ready, value-type API. Both compressed
) and uncompressed MusicXML files are supported.
IvorMXL’s syntactic core turns MusicXML bytes into a typed, round-trippable
Everything flows through a small, explicit pipeline of four value types, each a

carries two Boolean state flags that enforce the order of
the pipeline: a document must be normalized before it can be validated, and

abstract.text: The grace type indicates the presence of a grace note. The slash attribute for a grace note is yes for slashed
grace notes. The steal-time-previous attribute indicates the percentage of time to steal from the previous
note for the grace note. The steal-time-following attribute indicates the percentage of time to steal from the
following note for the grace note, as for appoggiaturas. The make-time attribute indicates to make time, not
steal time; the units are in real-time divisions for the grace note.
The typed-text type represents a text element with a type attribute.
The attributes element contains musical information that typically changes on measure boundaries. This
includes key and time signatures, clefs, transpositions, and staving. When attributes are changed mid-measure,
it affects the music in score order, not in MusicXML document order.
